title: Keying and Eviction Economics Playbook for Prefix Batching
creator: Mariela Ortega
description: Problem: We observe that small changes to cache key normalization and eviction heuristics produce non-linear cost and latency outcomes once batching interacts with prefix popularity distributions. Current guidance and autotuners are conservative and leave 10-20% unit cost on the table for mid-tail workloads. This ticket will produce a reproducible playbook for designing cache keys and eviction policies that are robust under batching and route-level traffic skew. Scope: key canonicalization rules, eviction economic model, per-prefix TTL annealing schedule, instrumentation required, and a safe apply/rollback procedure for production config changes.
proposed_solution: 1) Define canonical key transforms (token-level truncation, stemming rules for prefix groups, and affix normalization) and an opt-in per-route override map. 2) Build an 'eviction economics' model that predicts per-prefix marginal cost delta (tokens/saved and expected hitrate change) given batch-size distributions. Model inputs: prefix frequency histogram, sequence-length conditional distribution, existing TTL, and batch occupancy. 3) Implement a dry-run simulator that replays sampled traffic against candidate key/TTL configs and reports expected cost delta, p50/p95 latency shifts, and hit-rate lift per prefix. 4) Add staged apply: dry-run -> canary shadow (1% traffic, store diffs) -> graduated rollout (1%, 5%, 20%, 100%) with health gates on cost, p95 latency, and synthetic QA prompts. 5) Provide implementation knobs exposed via console and an API endpoint to propose recommendations and trigger safe applies/rollbacks.
experiment_plan: Phase A: Offline simulation using 14 days of sampled traffic (1% reservoir). Run 12 candidate key transforms and 8 TTL annealing schedules. Metrics collected: predicted token-cost delta, predicted hit-rate change per prefix, batch occupancy change, p50/p95 model latency delta. Phase B: Shadow canary on dedicated canary pool for 48 hours; gather real metric deltas and compare to simulator predictions. Phase C: Incremental rollout with automated rollback triggers. Success thresholds: >=8% median cost reduction for targeted routes OR >=12% for at least one high-cost route, with p95 latency regression <5ms, and no error-rate increase >0.1%.
rollout_plan: - Create recommendation artifact in Console with explanation and expected deltas. - Start with non-critical routes (internal metrics reasons) then expand. - Canary shadow: 1% of traffic mirrored to canary variant for 48h. - Gradual traffic shift if shadow signals match simulator within 10% error. - At each step run automated A/B tests comparing request cohorts; gate on cost & latency alerts. - Finalize by committing new defaults to runtime config and publish change log.
rollback_plan: Automated rollback triggers: (1) p95 latency increase > 5ms over baseline sustained for 5m, (2) cost per 1k tokens increases > 3% for 10m, (3) error rate increase >0.1% sustained for 5m. Rollback steps: pause rollout, cut traffic back to previous variant, mark config as 'reverted' with linked reason and simulation artifact, notify owners, and schedule postmortem within 48h. For partial regressions we will perform a staged roll-forward with narrowed prefix set or tweaked TTLs instead of full revert.
monitoring_and_alerting: Add per-variant dashboards: token cost per minute, tokens-per-batch, per-prefix hit-rate, p50/p95 latency, error rate. Synthetic probe set: 200 golden prompts covering critical prefixes to be run every 2m with assertions on quality and latency. Alerts: pager when rollback triggers fire; ephemeral slack channel for canary telemetry; monthly report summarizing realized vs predicted economics.
notes: 2026-02-20: Initial spike analysis shows three mid-tail prefixes (auth:, search:snippet, userprefs:) dominating cost growth under larger batchers.
2026-02-26: Prototype simulator implemented; early runs show simulator predicts cost delta within 12% of shadow data for stable prefixes.
